Sayyed Naushad Ali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5
January, 2026

Author: Subodh Abhyankar

Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:64

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Subodh Abhyankar
 On The 5 th Of January, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 51300 of 2025
 Sayyed Naushad Ali
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Avinash Sirpurkar - Senior Advocate with Shri Ba
 Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Hemant Sharma - G.A. for the State.
Shri Abhijeet Dubey- Advocate for the objector.
ORDER  1] They are heard.
Perused the case-diary.

2] This is the first application filed by the applicant  the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.875/2024 registered at Police Station Khajrana, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 376,
376(2)(n), 294, 506, 376(D), 354A, 450 and 201 of IPC.

3] Admittedly, the applicant was earlier granted anticipatory bail by the Trial Court itself on 11.11.2024, however, on an application filed by the prosecutrix for cancellation of bail on the ground that the applicant is threatening the prosecutrix, the bail has been cancelled vide the order dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:64 2 MCRC-51300-2025 31.10.2025, and thus, warrants have been issued against the applicant.

4] Learned senior counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case, as apparently, it was a case of consent, as the prosecutrix has a child,
who happens to be the son of the applicant only, and only on account of some dispute between the applicant and the prosecutrix, a false case has been registered.

It is also submitted that a legal notice Sayyed Naushad Ali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32223587/
1 was issued by the applicant to the prosecutrix on 23.01.2025, as the prosecutrix was posting objectionable post against the applicant on social media, however, soon after receipt of the aforesaid notice, an application for cancellation of bail was filed, which has been allowed vide the impugned order.

entities.text: Sayyed Naushad Ali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that there are no criminal antecedents, and the applicant has not misused the liberty extended to him by the Trial Court, and issuance of a legal notice cannot be termed as an act of threat.

It is further submitted that the prosecutrix is not appearing in the Trial Court, despite notice, and bailable warrants have been issued against her on 29.07.2025, and subsequently, arrest warrants have been issued on 31.10.2025.
Thus, it is submitted that the anticipatory bail application be allowed.

5] Prayer is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the objector, and it is submitted that even at the time when the prosecutrix had gone for the DNA test of her son, the applicant had threatened her in the presence of the police personnel.
Thus, it is submitted that no case for interference is made out.
6] Counsel for the State has also opposed the prayer.

7] Having considered the rival submissions, on perusal of the case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:64 3 MCRC-51300-2025 diary and the fact that the applicant was granted anticipatory bail by the Trial Court itself, and the applicant is also not denying the parenthood of the 9 year old son of the prosecutrix, and the fact that he has also issued a legal notice to the prosecutix, and there is no tangible material available on record to suggest that he, in any manner threatened the prosecutrix, this Court finds that the arrest of the applicant in such circumstances would not be necessary.
8] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
9] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed and disposed of.
C.c. as per rules.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Sayyed Naushad Ali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32223587/
